C005.subject: Intermittent fasting
C005.object: short-term weight loss (≤6 months) only in individuals with high baseline insulin resistance
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting short-term weight loss (≤6 months) only in individuals with high baseline insulin resistance]

[PATH:empirical] Re-analysis of existing intermittent fasting RCTs (e.g., TREAT, IF-PRO) stratified by baseline HOMA-IR or insulin sensitivity index — Directly tests the interaction between baseline insulin resistance and short-term weight loss outcome, using existing data to confirm or refute the subgroup effect.

[PATH:empirical] Prospective cohort or secondary analysis of dietary intervention trials (e.g., Look AHEAD or DPP) comparing intermittent fasting vs. continuous calorie restriction in participants with high vs. low HOMA-IR — Leverages large, well-characterized cohorts with measured insulin resistance to assess differential weight loss efficacy within 6 months.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials on intermittent fasting, with subgroup analysis by baseline insulin resistance (HOMA-IR >2.5 vs. ≤2.5) — Aggregates available evidence to quantify effect modification and assess consistency across studies, addressing the disputed status of the hypothesis.

C006.subject: Intermittent fasting
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting short-term weight loss (≤6 months)]

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing intermittent fasting (e.g., 5:2 diet, time-restricted eating) vs. continuous calorie restriction for weight loss at 3- and 6-month endpoints — A comprehensive synthesis of existing RCTs would directly test the hypothesis by pooling effect sizes and assessing heterogeneity, providing a high-confidence summary of whether intermittent fasting is ineffective for short-term weight loss.

[PATH:empirical] Secondary analysis of individual participant data from a large, multi-site RCT (e.g., CALERIE or similar) examining adherence patterns and weight trajectories in the first 6 months, stratified by fasting protocol and compliance levels — This would allow direct estimation of the causal effect of intermittent fasting on short-term weight loss while controlling for adherence, which is critical given the scope domain of 'short-term adherence'.

qualifier.temporal: within the first 6 months of adherence

C007.subject: Intermittent fasting with high protein intake during eating windows
C007.object: weight regain after 12 months compared to intermittent fasting alone
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting with high protein intake during eating windows weight regain after 12 months compared to intermittent fasting alone]

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing intermittent fasting with high protein intake vs. standard intermittent fasting, measuring body composition and weight at 12-month follow-up — Directly tests the hypothesis by comparing the two interventions under controlled conditions over the specified timeframe.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of dietary protein timing and amount on weight maintenance after caloric restriction — Synthesizes existing evidence on high protein intake and weight regain, providing a broader context to assess whether protein timing within intermittent fasting adds benefit.

[PATH:theoretical] Mechanistic study on the effects of high protein intake on appetite-regulating hormones (e.g., ghrelin, PYY) and energy expenditure during intermittent fasting — Explores biological plausibility: if high protein reduces hunger or increases thermogenesis, it may explain reduced weight regain, supporting or refuting the hypothesis.

C008.subject: Intermittent fasting
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting sustained weight loss after 12 months]

[PATH:empirical] Long-term randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intermittent fasting (e.g., 5:2 or time-restricted eating) with continuous calorie restriction over ≥12 months, with measured weight outcomes and attrition rates. — RCTs provide the strongest causal evidence for sustained weight loss, controlling for confounders and allowing direct comparison of IF versus standard dietary approaches.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort studies tracking adherence and weight change in free-living populations practicing intermittent fasting for ≥12 months. — Synthesizing existing observational data can reveal real-world effectiveness and identify factors (e.g., adherence, metabolic adaptation) that influence long-term weight maintenance, addressing the disputed status.

[PATH:theoretical] Mechanistic studies on metabolic and behavioral adaptations to intermittent fasting beyond 12 months, including changes in resting metabolic rate, gut microbiome, and eating behavior. — Understanding biological and psychological mechanisms can explain why IF may or may not lead to sustained weight loss, informing whether observed effects are plausible and generalizable across populations.

C011.subject: Intermittent fasting
C011.object: continuous calorie restriction with daily behavioral coaching
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting continuous calorie restriction with daily behavioral coaching]

[PATH:empirical] Long-term randomized controlled trial comparing intermittent fasting (e.g., 5:2 or time-restricted eating) versus continuous calorie restriction with daily behavioral coaching, with adherence tracking and weight measurements at 12, 18, and 24 months. — Directly tests the hypothesis by measuring long-term weight loss maintenance and adherence to fasting windows, which is the key condition in the qualifier.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on dietary adherence patterns in intermittent fasting versus continuous calorie restriction interventions lasting >12 months. — Synthesizes existing evidence on adherence declines (especially after 6 months) and their impact on weight loss outcomes, providing a broader empirical basis to confirm or refute the hypothesized effect.

[PATH:theoretical] Behavioral modeling study simulating the effect of declining adherence to fasting windows on energy balance and weight regain over 12–24 months, calibrated with empirical adherence data. — Tests the mechanistic plausibility of the qualifier by quantifying how much adherence decline would reduce the effectiveness of intermittent fasting relative to continuous calorie restriction with coaching.

scope.domain: long-term weight loss maintenance beyond 12 months

qualifier.condition: when adherence to fasting windows declines after 6 months

C012.subject: Intermittent fasting
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting long-term weight loss]

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials on intermittent fasting vs. continuous calorie restriction for weight maintenance at ≥12 months follow-up — Synthesizing existing long-term RCT data directly addresses whether intermittent fasting sustains weight loss beyond the initial intervention period, providing a high-level evidence base to confirm or refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Prospective cohort study with at least 24-month follow-up comparing adherence and weight trajectories among participants using intermittent fasting with dietary counseling vs. standard dietary counseling alone — Long-term observational data can capture real-world adherence patterns and weight regain, which are critical for assessing effectiveness in the specified domain of long-term weight loss with dietary counseling.

[PATH:theoretical] Mechanistic study on metabolic adaptations (e.g., resting metabolic rate, hormonal changes, gut microbiome) during prolonged intermittent fasting regimens beyond 6 months — Understanding biological compensatory mechanisms that may undermine long-term weight loss can provide theoretical support for or against the hypothesis, especially if metabolic slowdown or hormonal shifts are observed over time.

scope.domain: long-term weight loss with dietary counseling
